# Analysis overview

This extends from the preivous co-acessibility analysis in `/project/spott/cshan/fiber-seq/code/co-accessibility/LCL/CRE_co-accessibility_FIRE/LCL_co-access.Rmd`
I preivously used Fisher exact to test if the CRE pairs are more often co-accessible than expected, but there is high donor heterogeneity,
the CRE pairs accessible in one donor may not be accessible in another. This might be a problem because:

  - mixing donor creates an assoication

Permutation test shuffles CRE2 m6A proportions only within each sample

  - Each fiber (one sequenced DNA molecule) has a pair of numbers: its m6A proportion at CRE1 (prop1) and at CRE2 (prop2)
  - Within each sample, the permutation randomly reassigns the prop2 values among that sample’s fibers prop1 and the sample labels stay fixed


The `pooled` analysis includes all 31 samples and the `noXCI` analysis uses the existing noXCI results and sex assignments: chrX uses male samples only, and all other chromosomes use all 31 samples 

For each cCRE, `assemble_region_m6a(full_span = TRUE, positions = NULL)` builds one read × position matrix for the included samples - from this, we get positions with at least one observed m6A call among those pooled full span reads

Fraction of positions that methylated (counts positions with at least one observed m6a call across all pooled reads, reflects methylated positions out of observed positions)

  - `prop1 = rowSums(CRE1_matrix) / ncol(CRE1_matrix)` and `prop2 = rowSums(CRE2_matrix) / ncol(CRE2_matrix)`.

## Load the top ten co-accessible pairs (ranked by FDR)

Both top-ten sets are loaded from the tables saved by `LCL/CRE_co-accessibility_FIRE/LCL_co-access.Rmd` in `coaccess/`: 

  - `LCL_top10_pairs.tsv` (pooled) and `LCL_top10_pairs_noXCI.tsv` (female chrx removed)

```{r load-top-ten}
top10_files <- c(pooled = file.path(coaccess_dir, "LCL_top10_pairs.tsv"),
                 noXCI = file.path(coaccess_dir, "LCL_top10_pairs_noXCI.tsv"))
selected_sets <- setNames(lapply(analysis_sets, function(a) {
  chosen <- fread(top10_files[[a]])
  chosen[, `:=`(analysis = a, pair_rank = seq_len(.N))]
  chosen
}), analysis_sets)
selected <- rbindlist(selected_sets, fill = TRUE)

print(head(selected[, .(analysis, pair_rank, pair_id, CRE_pair, gene_names)]))
```

for a set of selected cCRE pairs, pull each pair’s per-sample count tables

  - extract pair information from `LCL_pair_sample_counts.tsv.gz`
  
```{r original-sample-counts}

# extract pair information 
read_selected_counts <- function(path, pair_ids) {
  con <- gzfile(path, "rt")
  on.exit(close(con))
  header <- readLines(con, n = 1L)
  out <- list()
  repeat {
    lines <- readLines(con, n = 100000L)
    if (!length(lines)) break
    ids <- substr(lines, 1L, regexpr("\t", lines, fixed = TRUE) - 1L)
    lines <- lines[ids %in% pair_ids]
    if (length(lines)) out[[length(out) + 1L]] <-
      fread(text = paste(c(header, lines), collapse = "\n"), sep = "\t")
  }
  rbindlist(out)
}
counts_file <- file.path(coaccess_dir, "LCL_pair_sample_counts.tsv.gz")
sample_counts <- read_selected_counts(counts_file, unique(selected$CRE_pair))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(sample_counts[, .(CRE_pair, sample_name)]),
          all(sample_counts$sample_name %in% samples),
          all(sample_counts$donor == sample_meta$donor[match(sample_counts$sample_name, samples)]),
          all(rowSums(as.matrix(sample_counts[, ..state_columns])) == sample_counts$n_shared_reads))

# pick which sample counts
  # if we are excluding female chrx, restrict it to male samples
pair_samples_for <- function(pair) {
  if (pair$analysis == "noXCI" && pair$chrom == "chrX") male_samples else samples
}

# subset to the CRE pair and the sample included
counts_for <- function(pair) {
  included <- pair_samples_for(pair)
  z <- sample_counts[CRE_pair == pair$CRE_pair & sample_name %in% included]
  stopifnot(nrow(z) == length(included), setequal(z$sample_name, included),
            all(z$chrom == pair$chrom))
  z <- copy(z[match(included, sample_name)])
  suffix <- if (pair$analysis == "noXCI") "_noXCI" else ""
  for (column in c(state_columns, "n_shared_reads"))
    if (sum(z[[column]]) != pair[[paste0(column, suffix)]])
      stop("Saved sample counts disagree with pooled Fisher table: ", pair$pair_id, " / ", column)
  z[, `:=`(analysis = pair$analysis, pair_id = pair$pair_id, pair_rank = pair$pair_rank)]
  z
}

selected_sample_counts <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(selected)), function(i) counts_for(selected[i])))

print(head(selected_sample_counts))
```

# Donor accessibility

For each donor, observed co-accessibility is `co_access`,  expected co-accessibility under independence is `(co_access + CRE1_access) * (co_access + CRE2_access) / N`, where `N` is the donor's total shared reads Fractions divide these counts by `N`

```{r donor-accessibility-summary}
# add the counts for each donor and each pair (each pair can have multiple donors)
donor_accessibility <- selected_sample_counts[, lapply(.SD, sum),
  by = .(analysis, pair_id, pair_rank, CRE_pair, donor),
  .SDcols = c(state_columns, "n_shared_reads")]

# calculate expected co-accessibility for each donor, and the fraction of CRE1/2 being accessible and the fraction of them co-accessible
donor_accessibility[, `:=`(
  observed_co_access = co_access,
  expected_co_access = fifelse(n_shared_reads > 0,
    expected_coaccess(co_closed, CRE1_access, CRE2_access, co_access), NA_real_))]
donor_accessibility[, `:=`(
  observed_fraction = fifelse(n_shared_reads > 0, co_access / n_shared_reads, NA_real_),
  expected_fraction = fifelse(n_shared_reads > 0, expected_co_access / n_shared_reads, NA_real_),
  observed_expected_ratio = fifelse(expected_co_access > 0, co_access / expected_co_access, NA_real_))]

# loop over "co_access", "CRE1_access", "CRE2_access", "co_closed" and calculate the fraction
for (state in state_columns)
  donor_accessibility[, (paste0(state, "_fraction")) :=
    fifelse(n_shared_reads > 0, get(state) / n_shared_reads, NA_real_)]

donor_states <- melt(donor_accessibility,
  id.vars = c("analysis", "pair_id", "pair_rank", "CRE_pair", "donor", "n_shared_reads"),
  measure.vars = state_columns, variable.name = "state", value.name = "n_fibers")
donor_states[, `:=`(config = factor(state_labels[as.character(state)], levels = CONFIG_LEVELS),
                    fraction = fifelse(n_shared_reads > 0, n_fibers / n_shared_reads, NA_real_))]

print(head(donor_states))
```

## calculate m6a (methylation) proportion at each selected pair

how much m6A methylation does each fiber have inside each cCRE? That makes it possible to test whether a fiber with high m6A at CRE1 also tends to have high m6A at CRE2, using continuous values rather than a binary open/closed call

`fiber_m6a_proportions()` and `assemble_region_m6a()` are from `parsing_footprints_functions.r`

for each selected pair, get the spanning reads and calculate m6a proportion at each CRE for every read

1. for each sample, query the sample's m6a for the CRE interval
2. a read is kept only if it covers the whole CRE
3. build reads x positions matrix
  - For each fiber, proportion = its m6A calls ÷ the number of positions with a call on any read


`per_fiber` contains the methylation proportion at each CRE separately for each read


```{r calculate-all-fiber-proportions}
fiber_results <- matrix_qc <- matrix_checks <- span_audits <- list()

# 1. per pair loop

# load the reads for each CRE
for (i in seq_len(nrow(selected))) {
  pair <- selected[i]
  included <- pair_samples_for(pair)
  message("Analysing ", pair$analysis, " / ", pair$pair_id)
  
  # Loads reads and FIRE data across the pair’s region for the included samples
  res <- load_region(list(chrom = pair$chrom, start = pair$region_start, end = pair$region_end),
    included, params$root, params$fire_root, fire_ver = "v0.1",
    tabix_bin = params$tabix, span_source = "aligned_blocks")
  
  # Labels each read: whether it covers both cCREs (shared) and whether each cCRE is accessible (acc1, acc2)
  labels <- label_reads(res,
    list(start = pair$cre1_start, end = pair$cre1_end),
    list(start = pair$cre2_start, end = pair$cre2_end),
    fire_overlap_fraction = fire_overlap_fraction)
  identity <- res$spans[, .(key, sample_name, original_RID = as.character(RID))]
  
  fibers <- merge(labels[shared == TRUE], identity,
                  by = c("key", "sample_name"), all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
  stopifnot(!anyNA(fibers$original_RID),
            !anyDuplicated(fibers[, .(sample_name, original_RID)]), all(fibers$shared))
  
  # add donor using sample metadata
  fibers[, `:=`(donor = sample_meta$donor[match(sample_name, samples)],
    state = fifelse(acc1 & acc2, "co_access", fifelse(acc1, "CRE1_access",
                    fifelse(acc2, "CRE2_access", "co_closed"))))]
  
  # Counts the four states per sample
  actual <- fibers[, .(co_access = sum(acc1 & acc2), CRE1_access = sum(acc1 & !acc2),
    CRE2_access = sum(!acc1 & acc2), co_closed = sum(!acc1 & !acc2), n_shared_reads = .N),
    by = sample_name]
  original <- counts_for(pair)
  for (column in c(state_columns, "n_shared_reads")) {
    values <- actual[[column]][match(original$sample_name, actual$sample_name)]
    values[is.na(values)] <- 0L
    if (!identical(as.numeric(values), as.numeric(original[[column]])))
      stop("Reloaded FIRE counts differ by sample for ", pair$pair_id, " / ", column)
  }
  
  # Subsets the sample table
  st <- sample_table[match(included, sample_table$sample_name), , drop = FALSE]
  
  # Builds a  region and calls fiber_m6a_proportions
  m <- lapply(1:2, function(j) {
    region <- data.frame(region_id = paste0(pair$pair_id, "_CRE", j), chr = pair$chrom,
      start = pair[[paste0("cre", j, "_start")]], end = pair[[paste0("cre", j, "_end")]])
    
    # 2. m6a proportion for each CRE
    r <- fiber_m6a_proportions(st, region, fibers[, .(sample_name, original_RID, donor, state)])
    ids <- list(analysis = pair$analysis, pair_id = pair$pair_id,
                CRE_pair = pair$CRE_pair, CRE = paste0("CRE", j))
    lapply(r, function(x) x[, (names(ids)) := ids][])
  })
  for (j in 1:2) {
    z <- m[[j]]$fibers[, .(sample_name, original_RID, status, n_m6a_calls, proportion, n_positions)]
    setnames(z, c("status", "n_m6a_calls", "proportion", "n_positions"),
      c(paste0("CRE", j, "_status"), paste0("m6a_calls", j), paste0("prop", j), paste0("n_positions", j)))
    fibers <- merge(fibers, z, by = c("sample_name", "original_RID"), all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
  }
  fibers[, `:=`(analysis = pair$analysis, pair_id = pair$pair_id, pair_rank = pair$pair_rank,
    CRE_pair = pair$CRE_pair, chrom = pair$chrom,
    qualifying = CRE1_status == "retained" & CRE2_status == "retained" & is.finite(prop1) & is.finite(prop2))]
  setorder(fibers, sample_name, original_RID)
  fiber_results[[i]] <- fibers
  matrix_qc[[i]] <- rbind(m[[1]]$qc, m[[2]]$qc)
  matrix_checks[[i]] <- rbind(m[[1]]$checks, m[[2]]$checks)
  span_audits[[i]] <- rbind(m[[1]]$fibers, m[[2]]$fibers)
}
per_fiber <- rbindlist(fiber_results)
matrix_qc <- rbindlist(matrix_qc)
matrix_checks <- rbindlist(matrix_checks)
span_audit <- rbindlist(span_audits)
exclusions <- per_fiber[, .(n_fisher_fibers = .N, n_qualifying = sum(qualifying),
  n_excluded = sum(!qualifying),
  n_CRE1_full_span_excluded = sum(CRE1_status == "excluded_full_span"),
  n_CRE2_full_span_excluded = sum(CRE2_status == "excluded_full_span"),
  n_either_full_span_excluded = sum(CRE1_status == "excluded_full_span" | CRE2_status == "excluded_full_span"),
  n_CRE1_missing_ft_record = sum(CRE1_status == "missing_ft_record"),
  n_CRE2_missing_ft_record = sum(CRE2_status == "missing_ft_record")),
  by = .(analysis, pair_id, pair_rank, donor, sample_name)]

pair_attrition <- exclusions[, lapply(.SD, sum), by = .(analysis, pair_id, pair_rank),
  .SDcols = setdiff(names(exclusions), c("analysis", "pair_id", "pair_rank", "donor", "sample_name"))]


head(print(per_fiber))
```

calculate the average m6a proportion at each CRE for each pair

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `analysis` | Which analysis the pair belongs to. `noXCI` = chrX pairs use male samples only; all other chromosomes use all 31 samples. The other value is `pooled` (all 31 samples everywhere). |
| `pair_id` | Unique label for the pair within the analysis. It appears to encode the analysis, rank (`top1`, `top2`, ...), chromosome, and the start and end of the pair's genomic region. |
| `pair_rank` | The pair's rank (1 to 10) within its analysis, from the earlier co-accessibility testing. It matches the `top#` in `pair_id`. |
| `CRE_pair` | The two cCRE IDs joined by `-` (CRE1 first, then CRE2). Each ID ends with the cCRE class: `PLS` promoter-like, `pELS` proximal enhancer-like, `dELS` distal enhancer-like, `CA-TF` chromatin accessible with TF binding, `CA` chromatin accessible. |
| `n_fibers` | Number of qualifying fibers for the pair: fibers covering both cCREs and spanning both fully, so m6A could be computed at both. This is the count behind both means. |
| `mean_prop1` | Average m6A proportion at CRE1 across those fibers. Each fiber's proportion = its m6A calls at CRE1 ÷ `n_positions1`. |
| `mean_prop2` | Average m6A proportion at CRE2 across those fibers, using `n_positions2`. |
| `n_positions1` | CRE1 denominator: number of positions in CRE1 with an m6A call on at least one full-span read, pooled over the analysis's samples. Not the cCRE width or the A/T count. |
| `n_positions2` | CRE2 denominator, defined the same way. |

**Notes**

- Means are per fiber, not per donor
- Each cCRE has its own denominator, so proportions are not directly comparable across pairs

```{r methylation-summaries}
# mean_props() and complete_summary() come from stats_testing_functions.r

qualifying <- per_fiber[qualifying == TRUE]
pair_keys <- c("analysis", "pair_id", "pair_rank", "CRE_pair")
pair_grid <- unique(selected[, ..pair_keys])
pooled_means <- complete_summary(pair_grid, mean_props(qualifying, pair_keys), pair_keys)
state_grid <- pair_grid[, .(state = state_columns), by = pair_keys]
state_keys <- c(pair_keys, "state")
state_means <- complete_summary(state_grid, mean_props(qualifying, state_keys), state_keys)
donor_keys <- c(pair_keys, "donor")
donor_grid <- unique(selected_sample_counts[, ..donor_keys])
donor_means <- complete_summary(donor_grid, mean_props(qualifying, donor_keys), donor_keys)
denominators <- unique(per_fiber[, .(analysis, pair_id, n_positions1, n_positions2)])
stopifnot(nrow(denominators) == nrow(selected))
pooled_means <- merge(pooled_means, denominators, by = c("analysis", "pair_id"))
state_means <- merge(state_means, denominators, by = c("analysis", "pair_id"))
donor_means <- merge(donor_means, denominators, by = c("analysis", "pair_id"))

print(pooled_means[order(analysis, pair_rank)])
```

# Permutation test on methylation proportion

test statistic is Spearman correlation across all fibers in a pair. Each of 10,000 permutations shuffles CRE2 proportions within the same sample, while CRE1 proportions and sample identity remain fixed

The empirical one-sided p-value for positive association is
`(1 + sum(permuted_rho >= observed_rho)) / (10000 + 1)`

- BH correction uses the ten primary tests within each selected analysis set.

`permute_pooled_spearman()` is sourced from `stats_testing_functions.r`


within a sample, does a fiber with more m6A at CRE1 also have more at CRE2? 

I calculated this using spearman rank correlation (p - rho), which measures how consistently two variables rise and fall together, using their ranked order, and in this case, this is the average methylation proportion at CRE1/2. I used the formula with tied ranks 

 - p = +1: fibers with higher CRE1 m6A always have higher CRE2 m6A
 - p = 0: no relationship
 - p = −1: higher CRE1 always goes with lower CRE2
 

Observed rho - calculated once from counts
1. rank CRE1/2 methylation proportion, ties get the average of their ranks
2. center each rank by substracting the mean rank, c = rank - mean rank
3. numerator = for each fiber, multiply its two centered ranks, then add up. If a fiber is above average at both cCREs (+ × +) or below at both (− × −), the product is positive. If it’s high at one and low at the other, the product is negative. A large positive sum means the two tend to agree
4. denominator = square root of of the sum of c1 x c2

null rho
1. shuffle CRE2 ranks within each sample, recompute rho, and repeat 10,000 times to get 10,000 null rhos.
2. count how many null rhos are at least as large as the observed rho.
3. apply the formula: p = (1 + #{null rho ≥ observed rho}) / (1 + 10,000)


since we have different samples, i calculated pooled p and adjusted p

- pool p = centered on overall mean rank across all fibers
- adjusted p = each sample's own mean rank

each permutation gives one rho, and we count how many null rhos are at least as large as the observed rhom and calculate p value


```{r run-permutations}
permutation_results <- permutation_nulls <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(selected))) {
  pair <- selected[i]
  d <- per_fiber[analysis == pair$analysis & pair_id == pair$pair_id & qualifying == TRUE]

  pair_seed <- as.integer(params$seed + pair$pair_rank + if (pair$analysis == "noXCI") 1000L else 0L)
  
  # Runs the test (10,000 permutations). It returns a list with fit$statistics (observed rho, adjusted rho, p-values, null mean and SD, a status) and fit$null (the null values from the shuffles)
  fit <- permute_pooled_spearman(d, n_permutations = params$n_permutations, seed = pair_seed)
  s <- as.data.table(fit$statistics)
  s[, `:=`(analysis = pair$analysis, pair_id = pair$pair_id,
            pair_rank = pair$pair_rank, CRE_pair = pair$CRE_pair)]
  n <- as.data.table(fit$null)
  n[, `:=`(analysis = pair$analysis, pair_id = pair$pair_id, pair_rank = pair$pair_rank)]
  permutation_results[[i]] <- s
  permutation_nulls[[i]] <- n
}

permutation_statistics <- rbindlist(permutation_results)
permutation_null <- rbindlist(permutation_nulls)

# Multiple-testing correction
permutation_statistics[, `:=`(bh_family_size = 10L,
  p_positive_BH = adjust_bh(p_positive, n = 10L),
  adjusted_p_positive_BH = adjust_bh(adjusted_p_positive, n = 10L)), by = analysis]
permutation_statistics <- merge(permutation_statistics, pair_attrition,
  by = c("analysis", "pair_id", "pair_rank"))
permutation_statistics <- merge(permutation_statistics, denominators, by = c("analysis", "pair_id"))
setorder(permutation_statistics, analysis, pair_rank)

print(permutation_statistics)
```

### methylation proportion after permutation

scattorplot to show if the CRE pairs m6a levels move together on the same read, and if the pooled rho is close to the adjusted within sample rho

- if they are close, the correlation comes from variation among fibers within samples. If adjusted is much lower, part of the trend is that some samples are simply more methylated at both cCREs, which the permutation test accounts for

```{r scatterplots, fig.height=11}
if (isTRUE(params$make_plots)) for (a in analysis_sets) {
  d <- copy(qualifying[analysis == a])
  d[, `:=`(pair_id = factor(pair_id, levels = selected_sets[[a]]$pair_id),
            config = factor(state_labels[state], levels = CONFIG_LEVELS))]
  s <- copy(permutation_statistics[analysis == a])
  s[, pair_id := factor(pair_id, levels = selected_sets[[a]]$pair_id)]
  s[, label := sprintf("n=%d | rho=%.3f\nadjusted rho=%.3f | BH p=%.3g",
    n_qualifying, spearman_rho, within_sample_adjusted_rho, p_positive_BH)]
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(prop1, prop2, colour = config)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.8, alpha = 0.4) +

              hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 2.6) +

  print(p)
  queue_plot(p, paste0(a, "_per_fiber_m6a_scatter"), height = 11)
}
```

### null distribution for each CRE pair

- histogram: the 10,000 rho values from shuffling CRE2 within samples. This is what correlation expect by chance
- red line:  observed rho from counts


p-value is the fraction of the histogram at or beyond that line --> stronger evidence further away from the histogram

distribution of the histogram

- Centered near 0: the pair has little sample-level structure
- Centered well above 0: samples differ systematically, with some high at both cCREs and some low at both

```{r permutation-null-plots, fig.height=15}
if (isTRUE(params$make_plots)) for (a in analysis_sets) {
  d <- melt(permutation_null[analysis == a],
    id.vars = c("analysis", "pair_id", "pair_rank", "permutation"),
    measure.vars = c("spearman_rho", "within_sample_adjusted_rho"),
    variable.name = "statistic", value.name = "rho")
  s <- permutation_statistics[analysis == a]
  lines <- rbind(
    s[, .(pair_id, statistic = "spearman_rho", observed = spearman_rho,

  for (z in list(d, lines)) {

    z[, statistic := factor(statistic, levels = c("spearman_rho", "within_sample_adjusted_rho"),
      labels = c("Pooled Spearman", "Sample-adjusted rank correlation"))]
  }
  lines[, label := fifelse(is.finite(observed),
    sprintf("observed %.3f | BH p %.3g", observed, adjusted_p), paste("Undefined:", status))]
  p <- ggplot(d[is.finite(rho)], aes(rho)) +

              hjust = -0.03, vjust = 1.2, size = 2.6) +
    facet_grid(pair_id ~ statistic, scales = "free", drop = FALSE,
      labeller = labeller(pair_id = function(x)
        sub("_(chr[^_]+)_([0-9]+)_([0-9]+)$", "\n\\1:\\2-\\3", x))) +
    labs(x = "Correlation after within-sample CRE2 shuffle", y = "Permutations",

  print(p)
```

### Empirical permutation p-value 

Plot 1: Histogram
  - x-axis: nominal p-value, from 0 to 1 in bins of 0.05
  - y-axis: number of shuffled datasets in each bin
  - converts each rho into the usual one-sided t-test p-value, with t = r·√((n−2)/(1−r²)) and n − 2 degrees of freedom

From the distribution, it seems like the the nominal p-values are too small

Plot 2: QQ plot
  - x-axis: the expected −log10(p) if the p-values were uniform. For the i-th ranked draw out of N, that is −log10((i − 0.5)/N)
  - y-axis: the observed −log10(nominal p) for that draw, with the smallest p-values aligned to the largest expected values

```{r shuffled-p-value-diagnostics, fig.height=13}
null_p_diagnostics <- merge(
  permutation_null[, .(analysis, pair_id, pair_rank, permutation, spearman_rho)],
  permutation_statistics[, .(analysis, pair_id, n_paired_finite_fibers)],
  by = c("analysis", "pair_id"))
# turns each shuffled rho into the log of a one-sided t-test p-value
null_p_diagnostics[, log_p := spearman_nominal_logp(spearman_rho, n_paired_finite_fibers)]
null_p_diagnostics[, nominal_p := exp(log_p)]


for (a in analysis_sets) {
  d <- copy(null_p_diagnostics[analysis == a])
  labels <- d[, .(label = paste0(pair_id[1], "\nvalid = ", sum(!is.na(log_p)),
    "; unavailable = ", sum(is.na(log_p)))), by = .(pair_id, pair_rank)]
  setorder(labels, pair_rank)
  d[, panel := factor(pair_id, levels = labels$pair_id, labels = labels$label)]
  valid_d <- d[!is.na(log_p)]
  if (!nrow(valid_d)) next
  
  
  p <- ggplot(valid_d, aes(nominal_p)) +
    geom_histogram(breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.05), colour = "white", fill = "steelblue") +
    facet_wrap(~ panel, ncol = 2, drop = FALSE) +
    labs(x = "Permutation p-value (nominal spearman)", y = "Frequency",
         title = paste(a, "- p-values from shuffled datasets")) +
    theme_bw()
  print(p)
  queue_plot(p, paste0(a, "_shuffled_p_value_histograms"), height = 13)
  setorder(valid_d, pair_rank, log_p, permutation)
  valid_d[, expected := -log10((seq_len(.N) - 0.5) / .N), by = pair_id]

  valid_d[, observed := -pmax(log_p, log(.Machine$double.xmin)) / log(10)]
  p <- ggplot(valid_d, aes(expected, observed)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
    geom_point(size = 0.45, alpha = 0.35) +
    facet_wrap(~ panel, ncol = 2, scales = "free", drop = FALSE) +
    labs(x = "Expected -log10(p-value)", y = "Observed -log10(shuffled nominal p-value)",
         title = paste(a, "- shuffled-dataset p-value QQ plots"),
         subtitle = "All valid draws; displayed -log10(p) capped at machine precision") +
    theme_bw()
  print(p)
  queue_plot(p, paste0(a, "_shuffled_p_value_qq"), height = 13)
}
```
